healthy.description: The model associates this image with a healthy training category. This does not rule out early infection, pests, nutrient stress or problems outside the supported categories.
symptoms: No supported disease pattern was selected; inspect the whole plant as well as this leaf.
prevention: Continue regular observation and use crop-appropriate watering, spacing and hygiene.
Seek local agricultural advice if symptoms persist or spread.

Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease affecting apple leaves and fruit, favored by wet conditions.
symptoms: Olive to dark leaf spots, sometimes with a velvety surface.
Leaf distortion or early leaf fall.
prevention: Manage fallen infected leaves.
Choose locally suitable resistant cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that can affect leaves, fruit and woody tissues.
symptoms: Circular leaf lesions with darker borders and lighter centers.
Fruit decay or dead and cankered branches.
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and dead infected wood using locally recommended sanitation practices.
Inspect trees and avoid unnecessary bark injury.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A rust fungus alternating between apple relatives and juniper hosts.
symptoms: Yellow to orange-red leaf spots.
Small dark dots above spots and tube-like structures below.
prevention: Use resistant apple cultivars where available.
Review nearby juniper hosts with a local adviser; separation can reduce exposure.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease producing powdery growth on susceptible tissues.
symptoms: White or gray powder-like growth on leaves.
Distorted young foliage or affected shoots.
prevention: Monitor susceptible new growth.
Use locally appropriate cultural management and seek guidance before treatment.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal foliar disease favored by extended humidity and infected corn residue.
symptoms: Gray or tan rectangular lesions bounded by leaf veins.
Small early spots that enlarge and merge.
prevention: Choose resistant hybrids.
Use appropriate crop rotation and residue management.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal rust that forms spore pustules on corn foliage.
symptoms: Rust-brown elongated pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Pustules darken with age; severe infection may yellow leaves.
prevention: Select resistant hybrids.
Scout leaves during favorable cool, wet weather.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease causing elongated necrotic lesions on corn leaves.
symptoms: Long canoe-shaped gray-green to tan lesions.
Larger areas of dead foliage when lesions join.
prevention: Choose resistant hybrids and appropriate rotations.
Assess residue and local disease history with an extension adviser.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease affecting green tissues and fruit; infected mummified berries can carry inoculum.
symptoms: Round brown leaf spots with dark margins and small black dots.
Berries shrivel into dark mummies.
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and infected prunings before new growth.
Consider resistant varieties suited to the area.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex of wood-associated fungal diseases with variable leaf and fruit symptoms.
symptoms: Interveinal red or yellow striping that becomes necrotic.
Dark spots may occur on berries; symptoms vary between years.
prevention: Use clean planting material.
Discuss pruning-wound protection and trunk-disease management with a viticulture specialist.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.disease_name: Grape leaf blight / Isariopsis leaf spot
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal leaf disease associated with Pseudocercospora vitis, also known as Isariopsis clavispora. Older leaves are often affected in warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Irregular reddish-brown spots that darken, sometimes surrounded by a yellow or pale-green halo.
Brown tissue and fungal structures may be visible on the lower leaf surface.
prevention: Monitor mature leaves during humid weather and document changes for a grape disease adviser.
Confirm the cause with a local agricultural specialist before choosing disease-specific management.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A serious bacterial citrus disease associated with psyllid vectors. An image cannot confirm infection.
symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy yellow mottling on leaves.
Small, irregularly shaped fruit and decline of growth.
prevention: Obtain clean nursery stock and monitor psyllids.
Seek local plant-health confirmation and follow applicable guidance on moving citrus material.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease of stone fruits that affects foliage, shoots and fruit.
symptoms: Small angular, water-soaked leaf spots whose centers may fall out.
Severe infection can yellow leaves; fruit may become pitted or cracked.
prevention: Choose locally suitable resistant peach cultivars.
Ask a local fruit extension specialist to confirm the cause and advise on orchard management.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that can spread through infected planting material and splashing water.
symptoms: Small dark or water-soaked leaf spots.
Lesions can merge and affected leaves may drop.
prevention: Use disease-free seed and transplants.
Reduce foliage wetness and avoid handling plants while wet.

Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease often beginning on older foliage.
symptoms: Brown leaf spots with concentric rings.
Yellowing around lesions and eventual leaf death.
prevention: Reduce prolonged foliage wetness.
Use rotation, sanitation and crop-appropriate nutrition.

Potato___Late_blight.description: A potentially fast-spreading disease caused by the water mold Phytophthora infestans.
symptoms: Irregular olive-brown, water-soaked leaf lesions.
White growth may appear in humid conditions; tubers can also be affected.
prevention: Use healthy planting material and manage volunteer plants.
Monitor local alerts and seek prompt expert confirmation of suspected outbreaks.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A common fungal disease of cucurbit foliage.
symptoms: White powder-like patches on leaves or petioles.
Affected foliage may yellow and die early.
prevention: Choose resistant varieties when suitable.
Monitor foliage from vegetative growth through fruiting.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal leaf disease that can be difficult to distinguish from other strawberry leaf spots.
symptoms: Numerous dark purplish spots and scorched-looking foliage.
prevention: Use healthy plants and manage infected leaf debris.
Provide appropriate spacing and seek confirmation when leaf symptoms overlap.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease affecting tomato leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Small dark leaf lesions, sometimes with yellow halos.
Fruit may develop raised or corky spots.
prevention: Use healthy seed and transplants.
Reduce splashing and avoid working with wet foliage.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease commonly beginning on lower, older leaves.
symptoms: Brown target-like lesions with concentric rings.
Yellowing around lesions and progressive loss of affected leaves.
prevention: Improve airflow, use mulch and water at the base.
Rotate crops and manage infected residue.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A rapidly spreading disease caused by a water mold, favored by cool, wet conditions.
symptoms: Irregular water-soaked lesions that turn brown.
White sporulation may be visible in humid weather; stems and fruit may be affected.
prevention: Inspect transplants and monitor local disease alerts.
Reduce prolonged leaf wetness and seek prompt agricultural advice.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease often associated with humid greenhouses and high tunnels.
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces.
Olive-brown velvety growth below corresponding patches.
prevention: Ventilate and space plants to reduce humidity.
Use drip irrigation and clean up crop residues.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot often beginning on lower tomato leaves.
symptoms: Small round lesions with pale centers and dark margins.
Tiny dark fungal structures may appear inside lesions.
prevention: Mulch and water at the plant base to reduce splash.
Improve spacing and remove affected crop debris appropriately.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Mite feeding damage, rather than a pathogen disease, included as a PlantVillage category.
symptoms: Fine pale stippling, yellowing or bronzing.
Fine webbing and mites may occur beneath leaves.
prevention: Avoid water stress and preserve natural enemies.
Inspect leaf undersides and confirm mites before taking action.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola; leaf symptoms overlap with other spots.
symptoms: Small dark lesions expanding to pale centers with darker rings.
Lesions may merge, and fruit can develop pitted lesions.
prevention: Use crop sanitation and reduce conditions favoring prolonged leaf wetness.
Confirm the cause before selecting disease-specific management.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease spread by whiteflies and movement of infected plants.
symptoms: Small upward-curled leaves with yellow margins or interveinal yellowing.
Stunted growth and reduced fruit set.
prevention: Use clean transplants and locally suitable resistant varieties.
Monitor whiteflies and manage volunteer hosts with local IPM guidance.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A viral disease requiring laboratory confirmation because visible symptoms overlap with other causes.
symptoms: Alternating light and dark green leaf mottling.
Distorted leaves and stunting may occur.
prevention: Use clean seed and transplants.
Practice hand and tool hygiene to reduce mechanical spread.
